reply_text:
Reviewed `excerpt-helper` against `main` at `59856d7`. **I’d fix these before merging:**

1. **Short text gets truncated and always receives an ellipsis** — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no check for text that already fits. `excerpt('hello world', 50)` returns `"hello…"` instead of `"hello world"`; an empty string returns `"…"`. This contradicts the README’s unchanged-text and ellipsis-only-when-removed guarantees.

2. **The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering** — `src/card.js:1–2` (unchanged)  
   `card()` still returns only `entry.body.trim()`. Neither new helper is called anywhere outside tests, so cards continue displaying the full Markdown body rather than a plain-text preview. The branch needs an integration point and an end-to-end card test.

3. **A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily discarded** — `src/words.js:2–3`  
   Slicing before searching excludes a space at index `limit`. For example, `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `"one…"` even though `"one two"` fits exactly. The existing words test actually locks in this off-by-one behavior.

4. **Markdown conversion deletes literal content and leaves common markup behind** — `src/plain.js:3–4`  
   Removing every `_`, `*`, `~`, and backtick is not equivalent to removing Markdown delimiters: `snake_case` becomes `snakecase`. Meanwhile, `# Heading` retains its heading marker and `![alt](img.png)` becomes `!alt`. This can corrupt ordinary preview text while still exposing Markdown syntax.

**Validation:** All four existing tests pass, but they miss these cases. I reproduced the examples above directly. No files changed.
